title: key={currentPage} was written inside the className string, so the page-turn animation never replays
detail: `className="animate-in fade-in slide-in-from-bottom-4 duration-700 key={currentPage}"` — the key is a literal substring of the class list, not a JSX prop. React therefore reuses the same element across page changes and the entrance animation runs exactly once, on first mount. The literal text is also emitted as two junk CSS classes.

title: The reader is a full-screen overlay with no focus trap, no role, and no Escape handler
detail: Every other overlay in the app went through useFocusTrap in Phase 2. This one did not: Tab walks out into the library behind it, Escape does nothing, and it announces as a plain div. It is the single most immersive surface in the product and the least accessible.

title: The reader always opens in light theme even when the app is in dark mode
detail: useState<Theme>('light') ignores the app-level theme entirely, so a user reading at night gets a full-screen white page. The reader keeping its own light/sepia/dark control is a reasonable decision; defaulting it against the user's stated preference is not.

title: Reading position, theme and font size all reset on every open
detail: All three are local component state with no persistence. Closing and reopening a long summary returns you to page 1 at the default size — the '% Complete' indicator is computed and displayed but never stored.

title: Theme and font-size controls are icon-only with no accessible name or pressed state
detail: Six toggle buttons carry no aria-label and no aria-pressed, so a screen reader announces six unlabelled buttons with no indication of which is active. The theme swatches also set colours via inline style, bypassing the design tokens used everywhere else.

title: formatInline is duplicated verbatim between EReader and BookDetail
detail: Two copies of the same inline-markdown splitter, neither in lib/, neither tested. They have already drifted — BookDetail's applies text colours, EReader's uses inherit/opacity.

title: Two different markdown renderers produce different output for the same content
detail: RenderFormattedContent supports blockquotes, numbered lists and drop caps; BookDetail's SummaryRenderer supports none of them but does support paragraph grouping on blank lines, which this one does not. The same summary text renders differently depending on which screen you are on.

title: Numbered-list detection mis-parses decimals at the start of a line
detail: /^\d+\./ matches '1.5 million people…', which is then rendered as list item number 1 with the remainder as its body.

title: No keyboard paging in a reading surface
detail: Arrow keys, PageUp/PageDown and Space do nothing; turning a page requires clicking one of two small footer buttons.
